cheng: Heads-up — perf regression observed after the kernel-routing tweak (last week). CPU-side flame shows tokenization + scheduler wakeups spike. Repro command and capture below, attaching nsys and perf output.

cheng: Repro capture I ran:
```
# on devbox
RT_BATCHING=0 KV_CACHE=0 perf record -F 99 -g -- ./redwood-serve --model gpt-small-8bit --max-tokens 512 --batch-size 8
nsys profile -o /tmp/nsys_run --sample=none --trace=cuda,osrt ./redwood-serve ...
```

perf-bot: nsys capture finished: /internal/artifacts/nsys/1943219999.nsys (2.3G) :file_folder:

maria: Did you confirm GPU kernels are not the culprit? nvprof/nsight shows kernel times stable?

cheng: GPU kernels look fine. nvprof shows kernel latencies ~same. CPU flamegraph (collapsed) points at two hotspots: `tokenize_bytes` (~28%) and `batch_scheduler::spin_wait` / futex wake paths (~12%). Also some time in `memmove` called per-token.

sam: Can you paste a small snippet from perf script collapsed stacks? Even top 20 lines help.

cheng: Sure — trimmed sample from `perf script` stacks (collapsed format):
```
python:tokenize_bytes;_PyObject_FastCall;batch_scheduler::enqueue;futex_wait
python:tokenize_bytes;_PyObject_FastCall;kv_cache::apply_prefix;memmove
python:tokenize_bytes;tokenize_inner;memcpy;memmove
batcher:try_schedule;batch_scheduler::spin_wait;futex_wake
```

irene: That second line rings a bell. I think the routing change added a fallback path that calls `kv_cache::apply_prefix` which in turn does per-token memmove when buffer layout differs. Before the change we preferred a bulk-copy kernel for contiguous input.

maria: Repro suggestion: try toggling RT_BATCHING=1 and also enable the `KV_CACHE=1` optimized path (the one that uses bulk copy) and compare perf. If the bug is per-token memmove we should see memmove drop and less scheduler churn.

cheng: Did a quick A/B. With RT_BATCHING=1 I see scheduler wakeups drop ~40% and memmove time shifts down ~60% for long prompts. KV_CACHE enabled helps for repeated prefixes but not initial cold requests. Metrics:
- RT_BATCHING=0 KV_CACHE=0: tokenize 28%, scheduler 12%, memmove 9%
- RT_BATCHING=1 KV_CACHE=0: tokenize 18%, scheduler 7%, memmove 6%
- RT_BATCHING=1 KV_CACHE=1: tokenize 15%, scheduler 5%, memmove 3%

cheng: Short root cause hypothesis: kernel-selector picks a safe fallback kernel when input alignment or token-chunk-size < N (code recently introduced to handle quantized/packed tensors). That fallback does per-token memcpy/memmove instead of one bulk memcpy. Combined with our batcher spin policy, it causes more wakeups and higher Python-level tokenization overhead.

sam: Makes sense. Two actionable items: (1) change kernel-selector policy to prefer bulk-copy when tokens_per_batch >= 16 (even if alignment is slightly off) and fallback to align-copy only if really necessary; (2) add a small microbench in perf CI: run tokenization flame and assert memmove % < X.

irene: I can dig up the exact patch that introduced the fallback — I recall a safety check on line around kernel_selector.cpp:242. Suggest a small patch: try memcpy with adjusted pointer arithmetic instead of per-token memmove; should be a cheap win.

maria: Also add a flamegraph smoke test to the PR so we detect regressions early. We had a similar regression slip earlier and it was caught late.

cheng: I'll draft a PR with: kernel-selector threshold change, a microbench reproducer, and a perf CI job. Quick patch diff I prototyped:
```
- for each token: memmove(dst + i*L, src + offsets[i], L)
+ // try single bulk copy when possible
+ if (is_contiguous(src, n_tokens)) memcpy(dst, src + start, total_len);
+ else for each token: memmove(...)
```

sam: sgtm. Please include perf output before/after in PR description and link to nsys capture. I can add CI failure threshold.

cheng: Will do. Thanks all. I'll post the PR and link back here when ready. :+1:
